end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from its source to the consumer.
Identified that food from 10 km away travels fewer food miles than food from 1500 km away.
Explained that longer journeys use more fuel and can cause more pollution.
Mentioned that longer travel can affect freshness and may require refrigeration.
Teach-back was not passed; comparison and full effects explanation need more practice.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles and comparing nearby and distant food sources. They explained the links between travel distance, fuel use, pollution, and freshness, and later gave a clear 10 km versus 1500 km example. There was an early mix-up about where bread comes from and whether all bread is the same; this became clearer when they described food miles from source to consumer, though the full explanation still needs another attempt. At home, ask Rohan to compare two foods by checking their labels and discussing which one likely travelled farther.
